name:
All right, I want to write specs for the current quest, which is the main quest, Zero of Sheaf Chat. I'm dictating through a microphone, so there might be some transcription errors. Let's go ahead and start documenting.

Okay, so what is the Sheaf Chat project? Sheaf Chat is a simple service that manages chats with Pi agents, each having a specific extension associated with them. In the Sheaf Chat project, we will provide a Pi agent extension along with a Node server that manages these extensions, as well as a web UI for chatting with Sheaf. First, I will describe the backend, then the browser UI.

The backend is a Node app that manages Pi agents. It lazily loads an agent when starting chats and offloads agents to disk if they haven't been used for a while, resuming them from their session files. The session files are stored in the data directory for Sheaf Chat, under a subdirectory called "piles." Sessions are organized into piles, and when you start a session, you specify which pile it belongs to. A pile is simply a subdirectory within the sessions directory. The piles directory itself is a subdirectory of the sessions directory inside the data directory for the Pi agent or Sheaf Chat. To start, resume, or reference a session, you use both the pile name and the session ID.

Each session should also include a manifest companion file alongside the JSONL file. This manifest stores metadata about the session, which we will discuss in more detail as we describe the sessions.

The agents should run completely independently of any machine or global Pi configuration. All Pi extensions and configurations should be provided by this repository and the chief chat server. Each session has a specified root directory. The agent is given a set of tools similar to the built-in tools, where all reads and writes are relative to the session's root directory. When specifying file names, they should be relative to the root directory, and all responses that would contain absolute paths come back relative to that root. There is no way to view or modify files outside that directory or its descendants. This restriction should be enforced at the tools layer. The agent must not be able to access anything outside its starting directory.  This extension should be implemented in the Sheaf Chat project.

When a new session starts, the first message should be sent to a side agent to generate a short description for that chat. The chat name and the root directory should be stored in the manifest to ensure the tools are set up correctly when resuming the chat.

For now, there will be two providers: OpenAI, requiring an OpenAI subscription, with its OAuth data stored in the project's data directory; and local inference. In the global configuration file for this repo, we'll have a key called local inference URL, and in the API keys file, a local API key. Models can be provided from either source. The available models should include the GPT models from OpenAI and those accessible at the local endpoint. We don't need to add any specific configuration for the local model setup, as that should already be handled.

The server should provide an interface for managing sessions, including listing existing sessions within a given pile, listing piles, creating new piles, starting new sessions, and resuming sessions. Starting a new session requires specifying a pile and then opening a WebSocket connection with a blank session after the user’s first message. The session description can be saved in a manifest file. The start session API should also accept the root directory as an argument.

When a session starts or is resumed, the user connects to a WebSocket protocol that exchanges AGUI messages. This protocol must also support control UI messages, such as requests for earlier messages when the user scrolls up to load previous content, and switches between models if AGUI does not natively support that.

Please write the detailed specification for this WebSocket protocol. It just needs to be sufficient to have a nice chat UI on the other side.

There is already a Python converter from wrapped Pi messages to AGUI messages located in the project quest runner, called AGUI_mapping.py. You can either reuse that or implement a new converter in TypeScript to handle Pi-to-AGUI message conversion.

When resuming a conversation with an agent using a session ID and a pile, there are two scenarios. Either an agent is already running and exists, allowing you to start a new WebSocket connection to that agent, or the session is stored as a file on disk. In the latter case, I want to create an agent by resuming that session file, then create a WebSocket that dispatches calls to this agent.

I also want to support multiple WebSockets connected to the same underlying agent. In this situation, any user message must be propagated to all connected clients. Incoming user messages should always steer the conversation; if there's an ongoing message, the new input should steer it. These messages must be visible across all chat interfaces.

When a conversation starts, the browser should request enough previous messages to populate the chat interface. Our goal is to keep the chat as robust and synchronized as possible.

There are already browser assets in projects/web for a chat interface. I want you to extend that. Currently, it doesn't support sending messages back, so that functionality needs to be added. It also lacks lazy loading for old messages, assuming everything loads upfront. For the existing uses, it should continue to work as is, but you should extend it to support both lazy loading and back-and-forth chat. I'll give you some leeway to define how that works since I don't have much front-end development experience.

mobile optimized is required.

A few final details. The chat service should be registered on port 9004. Everything needs to follow the directory structure in this repo. Please go ahead and specify everything accordingly.

I understand that you have a skill for finding the documentation for the Pi agent. If you could include a reference to that documentation in the specification, it would be helpful, since the agents implementing this spec won’t necessarily be Pi agents.
